Symptoms: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) can affect attention, learning, emotions, communication and movement. In adults it can involve difficulty concentrating, distractibility, forgetfulness, trouble organising or completing tasks, restlessness, impulsive actions, impatience and difficulty managing stress. ADHD symptoms occur regularly and can negatively affect more than one part of life, including education, work, relationships or social interaction.
Causes: The cause of ADHD is not known. A combination of factors may be involved. Factors linked with ADHD include having a parent or sibling with ADHD, autism or learning disability, epilepsy, premature birth, environmental factors and previous brain injury.
Warnings: There is no single test or checklist that can confirm ADHD. Symptoms and their impact need a full health assessment because concentration and related difficulties can also occur in other conditions. Speak to a GP practice if you think ADHD is having a negative effect on your life.
Recommendations: Management can begin with environmental and lifestyle changes. A healthcare professional may also discuss coaching, psychological therapy or medication when appropriate. Assessment and treatment choices should be made with a qualified healthcare professional.
